skills.title: Different Types of Families
skills.description: Families come in many shapes. Match each family, like one parent, blended, or foster, to its description.

skills.title: Groups in Our Community
skills.description: Your community has many groups. Pick the languages, foods, shops, and holidays that show this variety.

skills.title: Special Places on a Map
skills.description: Some places or countries matter to your family. Find them on a globe or map.

skills.title: Traditions and Celebrations
skills.description: Match celebrations like Diwali, Eid, Canada Day, or fall fairs to the group that celebrates them and what people do.

skills.title: Family Events in Order
skills.description: Put births, moves, and other family events in order from oldest to newest, like on a family tree or timeline.

skills.title: Passing On Heritage in Community
skills.description: Festivals, recipes, music, and dances pass culture to new generations. Match each event to what it shares.

skills.title: Passing On Family Heritage
skills.description: Families pass on culture through celebrations and practices, including First Nations, Métis, or Inuit ones. Pick how each one is passed on.

skills.title: Family Traditions Over Time
skills.description: Traditions can change across generations. Pick why, like moving to Canada, new technology, or colonization.

skills.title: Comparing Families and Traditions
skills.description: Compare different families and their celebrations. Sort what is the same and what is different.

skills.title: Traditions Then and Now
skills.description: Groups in your community celebrated differently in the past. Pick why traditions changed, like being outlawed or being given up.

skills.title: Reclaiming Indigenous Traditions
skills.description: Some traditions were banned or hidden because of colonization and residential schools. Pick how First Nations, Métis, and Inuit are bringing them back.

skills.title: Questions About Traditions
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate about how a celebration was done in the past and now.

skills.title: Sources About Traditions
skills.description: Photo albums, interviews, artefacts, and Elders' stories are sources. Sort which ones answer a question.

skills.title: Maps of Celebrations
skills.description: Read a map with a legend that shows where settlers came from or where celebrations happen.

skills.title: Venn Diagrams and Bar Graphs
skills.description: Use a Venn diagram or bar graph to see how family traditions are the same or different across generations.

skills.title: Conclusions About Traditions
skills.description: Look at the evidence and pick the conclusion about past and present traditions that it supports.

skills.title: Sharing Tradition Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share your findings and the right words like tradition, culture, generations, and celebration.

skills.title: Globes and Maps of the World
skills.description: Countries, continents, and water can be shown on globes, paper maps, and digital maps. Pick which one fits.

skills.title: Continents, Oceans, and the Equator
skills.description: Find continents, oceans, the equator, the poles, and hemispheres on a globe or map.

skills.title: North, South, East, West
skills.description: Use N, S, E, and W on a map to tell where a country, continent, or community is.

skills.title: Location and Climate
skills.description: Places close to the equator are warmer and places far from it are colder. Match places to their likely climate.

skills.title: Clues From Photos and Maps
skills.description: Look at photos and maps to pick where a place is and what its climate is like.

skills.title: Basic Needs Around the World
skills.description: People need food, water, clothing, shelter, and transportation. Match the ways communities meet each need.

skills.title: Communities Around the World
skills.description: Match communities, including a First Nation, Métis, or Inuit one, to their land, animals, homes, and culture.

skills.title: My Community and Another
skills.description: Sort what is the same and different between your community and one far away, like food, clothing, and homes.

skills.title: Lifestyles in Different Communities
skills.description: Compare how people in different parts of the world get food, shelter, and other needs.

skills.title: Adapting to Climate and Land
skills.description: People change how they dress, build, and live to fit hot, cold, or dry places. Match each adaptation to its place.

skills.title: Using Nature Wisely
skills.description: Using water, soil, and animals carefully keeps them for the future. Pick what happens when people do or do not use them wisely.

skills.title: Questions About Environment and Life
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate about how climate affects clothing, homes, or food.

skills.title: Gathering Facts About Communities
skills.description: Pick the best tool, like an atlas, a satellite image, a photo, or an Elder, to learn about a place and its people.

skills.title: Maps of Location and Lifestyle
skills.description: Use maps to see patterns, like how distance from the equator goes with climate, clothing, and shelter.

skills.title: Charts and Graphs About Climate
skills.description: Read a chart, bar graph, or pictograph, or look at photos, to tell which places have similar climates.

skills.title: Conclusions About Place and Life
skills.description: Use the evidence to pick the conclusion about how a place's nature and its people's ways of life are connected.

skills.title: Sharing Around-the-World Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share your findings and the right words like globe, equator, hemisphere, continent, and culture.
